title: What We Look for in Founders: determination, flexibility, imagination, naughtiness, friendship
summary: Paul Graham lists the five qualities Y Combinator looks for in founders. Determination matters most, balanced by flexibility. The other three are imagination, a naughty streak of beating the system, and a strong bond between cofounders. Each is illustrated with YC founders such as WePay, Greplin, Airbnb and Justin.tv.

principles.text: Past a basic intelligence threshold, determination matters most in founders, because you will hit many obstacles.
principles.quote: But as long as you're over a certain threshold of intelligence, what matters most is determination. You're going to hit a lot of obstacles.

principles.text: Pair determination with flexibility: stay set on the goal but be ready to change the plan, like a running back.
principles.quote: The world of startups is so unpredictable that you need to be able to modify your dreams on the fly.

principles.text: The most useful kind of intelligence is imagination: coming up with surprising ideas, since good startup ideas initially seem bad.
principles.quote: In the startup world, most good ideas seem bad initially. If they were obviously good, someone would already be doing them.

principles.text: Look for founders who beat the system. Breaking rules that don't matter is a good sign.
principles.quote: They delight in breaking rules, but not rules that matter.

principles.text: Ask founders about a time they hacked something to their advantage. It became one of YC's most-watched application questions.
principles.quote: He said to ask about a time when they'd hacked something to their advantage—hacked in the sense of beating the system, not breaking into computers.

principles.text: Cofounder friendship is essential: startups strain the relationship, so founders must genuinely like each other and work well together.
principles.quote: Startups do to the relationship between the founders what a dog does to a sock: if it can be pulled apart, it will be.
